findings.title: FIPS and non-FIPS providers have equal priority
findings.body: This provider returns order 200, the same as DefaultCryptoProvider and WildFlyElytronProvider. If a classpath contains both FIPS and non-FIPS provider services, the sort does not prefer the FIPS provider; the first service discovered wins. CryptoIntegration now silently accepts that configuration, so a FIPS deployment can select the non-FIPS implementation depending on service-resource order.

findings.title: Adding an abstract SPI method breaks existing provider implementations
findings.body: CryptoProvider is a public service-provider interface. An implementation compiled against the previous version can still be loaded by ServiceLoader, but it has no order() implementation; invoking this method during CryptoIntegration's sort then throws AbstractMethodError and prevents crypto initialization. Make this a default method or otherwise preserve compatibility with existing providers.

findings.title: The method returns a keystore provider instead of Bouncy Castle
findings.body: The CryptoProvider contract requires this method to return the Bouncy Castle provider, but this returns whichever provider implements the JVM's default keystore type (commonly SUN). Because this provider is registered for CryptoIntegration, consumers that use the returned provider for Bouncy Castle algorithms will instead use a provider that does not implement them and can fail with NoSuchAlgorithmException. Return an actual Bouncy Castle provider or represent its absence consistently.

findings.title: The selected provider makes signature operations fail unconditionally
findings.body: This implementation is registered as a CryptoProvider and can be the only provider discovered by a standalone authz-client deployment, but getSignature() always throws UnsupportedOperationException. Any authz-client or other Keycloak core code path that obtains signatures through CryptoIntegration—for example, a signed client-credentials JWT path using this SPI—will fail instead of obtaining a JCA Signature. The other unsupported SPI methods have the same limitation.

findings.title: Sequence parsing can read elements past the declared sequence boundary
findings.body: The loop tracks the sequence's declared length, but readNext() checks inner element lengths only against the entire input buffer. If an element extends past the remaining sequence bytes, readNext() consumes bytes after the sequence and the subtraction makes length negative, which ends the loop successfully. This accepts malformed DER and can interpret trailing bytes as sequence contents; reject any element whose encoded length exceeds the remaining sequence length.
